answer.description: The reply to what he said, in short plain English; or the one-sentence refusal for anything outside the Bible.

question.description: What he just said, put into clean written words: the capitals and punctuation it needs (question marks, full stops), the ums, uhs, repeated words and dropped starts taken out, the meaning and his own words kept. Never an answer or an explanation; unchanged when it was clean already. At most the length of what he said.

words.description: The Greek words the answer speaks about, each with its lemma and a short note that includes its parsing. Empty when the answer is about no particular word.

greek.description: The word as it stands in the text.

note.description: Its parsing and what it does here, in plain words.

syllables.description: Only when the question asked how to sound a word out (its focus kind is sound): the word's syllables in Greek letters, in order, each one short enough to say alone; for a Hebrew word (focus language he), in the pointed Hebrew letters. Leave it out otherwise.

transliteration.description: Only for a Hebrew word's sound question (focus kind sound and language he): how each entry of syllables sounds, in plain Latin letters with no special marks, in the same order and the same number, the stressed syllable in capitals (TSE, dek). Leave it out otherwise.

words_to_add.description: Only when he asked to put words on his words-to-learn list ('add σάρξ to my words'): the dictionary form of each word, in Greek letters. Leave it out otherwise.

study_way_line.description: Only in a quiz (mode quiz), and only when he asked for a lasting change to how he is quizzed ('shorter quizzes', 'skip the map', 'more grammar'): one short line, in his terms, that states the change as a standing instruction for later quizzes. The app shows it with a Keep this button and keeps it only if he taps; it is not kept otherwise. Leave it out for anything that is only for today.

quiz_goal_offer.description: Only in a quiz (mode quiz) with `quiz_goal` null and no `quiz_goal_once`, once you have understood why he wants the quiz: his goal in a few plain words of his own, at most 80 characters ('understanding what the passage says', 'learning Greek words'). The app shows it with Yes, from now on and Just this time buttons and keeps it as his Quiz goal only if he taps Yes. Leave it out once offered, when a goal is kept, and for anything else.

feedback_offer.description: Only when he asked for something Lampas does not do (to work with another app, a setting it does not have, a change to a screen): the one-line summary of his ask, in plain English and his terms, at most 200 characters. The app shows it as a Send this to the makers button under the answer and sends nothing unless he taps. Never a promise that the change will happen. Leave it out for anything else.

summary.description: One line saying what he wants.

setting_offer.description: Only when you propose a setting change he did not ask for outright (for example moving New words at to Frontier grammar): the one change, `key` and `value` as in `settings_changes`. The app shows it as a button, Change <setting>: <value>, and makes the change on his tap or when his next words are a yes (see `offer_reply`). A change he asked for outright goes in `settings_changes`. Leave it out for anything else.

key.description: A setting's key from the settings block.

value.description: The new value, as the settings block lists it.

offer_reply.description: Only when the request carried `pending_offer`, and only when his words are about that offer: 'confirm' when he says yes (the app then does exactly what a tap on the offer's button does), 'decline' when he says no (the offer is withdrawn and nothing is done), 'read_back' when he asks to hear it first (the offer stays; your answer speaks its exact text and asks for his yes). Leave it out for an ordinary question or when you are not sure: the offer then stays and nothing is done.

form_values.description: Only while he is being helped to fill in a form (`form` in the request): the values to put in its fields from what he just said, each the field's `name` and the field's whole new value. Only text and link fields, never pictures; never a field the form does not list. Leave it out when his words fill nothing.

value.description: The whole new value of the field.

form_ask.description: Only while he is being helped to fill in a form: the `name` of the field the question in `answer` is about (a pictures field when you ask for a photo). Leave it out when there is nothing more to ask, which is when every required field is filled and he has nothing to add.

links.description: Links the app turns into buttons that open a word or a verse in the reader's own study resources (lexicons, a Bible); he sees only the ones he has switched on. At most three. Leave it out when no lexicon or verse would help him.

lemma.description: The word's dictionary form, in Greek letters, with its accents and breathings.

reference.description: A verse of any book of the Bible, Old Testament or New, such as Romans 8:31, 1 John 1:9 or Isaiah 53:5.

go.description: Only when he asked, in words, to be taken to a chapter of the New Testament ('switch to Colossians 1', 'open John 3', 'take me to Romans 12'): the book and the chapter. The app opens the Reader there at once and says Opened; say in answer where you are taking him. Never for a chapter outside the 27 books of the New Testament, never on your own, and leave it out when he asked for no move.

book.description: The book's name exactly as in the list.

chapter.description: The chapter number, from 1 to the book's last chapter.

settings_changes.description: The settings he asked to change, each applied at once by the app. Only when he asked for the change in words, never on your own; only the keys and values the instructions list; leave it out when he asked for no change.
